## Install — no GitHub CLI, no tokens, no SSH keys

Download the **Source code (zip)** below, extract, and run the bundled installer. Same flow on every OS.

**macOS / Linux**
```bash
cd jtr-0.8.0
./install.sh
```

**Windows**
```powershell
cd .\jtr-0.8.0\
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\install.ps1
```

The installer fetches `uv` if needed, then runs `uv tool install` on the extracted source. See [INSTALL.md](https://github.com/BD-AI-SDLC/jtr/blob/main/INSTALL.md) for manual steps and troubleshooting.

## What's new

jtr now says out loud which Jira it speaks to, and stops you pointing it at one it doesn't.

- **Documented: Jira Server / Data Center only.** The README gained a **Supported Jira deployments** section. Nothing about the supported flavour was written down before, while the code had been committed to Server/DC all along — it sends Bearer PATs, calls `/rest/api/2/search`, and assigns by username. Jira Cloud needs Basic auth with an API token, `/rest/api/3/search/jql`, and `accountId`-based assignment, so it was never going to work.
- **Cloud base URLs are rejected up front.** Pointing jtr at `*.atlassian.net` (or `*.jira.com`) used to get you an opaque `HTTP 401` on your first real command, with nothing to suggest the URL itself was the problem. `jtr init` and `jtr config base-url` now refuse the URL before writing any config, and explain which four things differ. `--json` reports `"error": "unsupported_deployment"` rather than the misleading `"not_authenticated"`.
- **Vendor-neutral docs and examples.** Example hosts are now `tracker.example.com`, the sample project key is `PROJ`, and the sample context path is `/jira` — in the README, `INSTALL.md`, `EXAMPLES.md`, `.env.example`, the bundled `/jtr` skill, and the `jtr --help` text. Previously these carried one organization's tracker hostname and project key, which read as configuration rather than as placeholders.

WebSEAL and TFIM are still named throughout. They're IBM product names rather than site-specific ones, they match the text an affected user actually sees in an error, and the gateway-detection logic matches on them.

## Upgrading

Install as usual. No config, cookie, or `.env` changes are required, and existing setups keep working unchanged.

One behaviour change worth knowing: if your `JTR_BASE_URL` points at a Jira Cloud host, `jtr` now fails fast with an explanatory message instead of a 401. This only affects configurations that could not successfully complete a request in the first place.
